proposals.before: In the early Tonghe reign he earned the jinshi degree and was appointed a patrol officer in Lulong.
proposals.after: In the early Huitong reign he earned the jinshi degree and was appointed a patrol officer in Lulong.
proposals.reason: 會同 is the Huitong reign (AD 938–947), not 統和 Tonghe; the mistranslation contradicts the following Taizong/Tianlu career sequence.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Tonghe he passed the jinshi examination and became a patrol officer in Lulong.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Huitong he passed the jinshi examination and became a patrol officer in Lulong.
proposals.reason: 會同 must be rendered Huitong, not Tonghe (統和).

proposals.before: The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director/President of the Imperial Secretariat (Shangshu ling), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: The emperor sighed in grief, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: The emperor sighed in grief, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is not Grand Preceptor; correct the office title.

decisions.reason: Chinese 會同初 names the Huitong reign; Tonghe (統和) is a different later era, and the following Taizong/Tianlu sequence confirms Huitong.
Chinese 會同 must be Huitong, not Tonghe (統和); the literal field repeats the same era error as the idiomatic.
Chinese 贈尚書令 is a posthumous Shangshu ling appointment; Grand Preceptor would be 太師, so Director of the Imperial Secretariat is the correct office.
Chinese 尚書令 is not Grand Preceptor; correcting the literal title to Director of the Imperial Secretariat matches the source.
